title: NASA Jupiter satellite sheet: Io (I) mass 893.2×10^20 kg, radius 1821.5 km
summary: The Jupiter satellite fact sheet lists Io (I) at mass 893.2 × 10^20 kg and radius 1821.5 km.
body: NASA's Jupiter satellite fact sheet lists Io (I) with mass 893.2 × 10^20 kg, radius 1821.5 km, mean density 3530 kg/m^3, and visual geometric albedo 0.62. Orbital parameters on the same sheet: Semi-major axis (10 3 km) = 421.8; Semi-major axis (Jovian Radii) = 5.91; Orbital Period* (days) = 1.769138; Rotation Period (days) = S; Inclination (degrees) = 0.04; Eccentricity = 0.004. These are the cells printed on the sheet. The sheet does not say, on this row, which cells are a spacecraft measurement and which are an estimate. The sheet says R indicates retrograde motion, and S indicates synchronous rotation, the rotation period equal to the orbital period. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last Updated line: 6 December 2023.
